## Summary
A question tweet seeding four techniques for making AI-authored PRs easier to review, plus one "wildest" outlier:

1. **/show-me** (by @dexhorthy, Dex Horthy) — a command/skill for easy-to-read diffs.
2. **Describe the changes in pseudocode** — the PR narrates intent, not just the diff.
3. **Mermaid diagrams** — visualize control/data-flow changes.
4. **Evidence of TDD** — show tests failing first, then passing.
5. **The wildest version** (@dctanner's agent): uses Playwright to record a video of the frontend feature working, with text-to-speech narration over the top — "the agent literally talks you through its change." Review becomes watching a narrated demo instead of reading a diff.

## Why it matters
- **Third leg of the vault's agent-workflow cluster:** existing nodes police *planning* (Phelps loop: converge the PRD before code) and *execution* (Scope Guard rules, complexity gates, ponytail review hook). This is the *review* leg — making agent output legible to the human at PR time.
- **One principle under all the techniques:** shift the reviewer from reading raw diffs to reading intent-first artifacts — what changed (pseudocode, Mermaid, readable diffs), why it's correct (TDD evidence), or proof it works (Playwright-narrated demo). Same "review must be structural, not vibes" instinct as the Quentin code-quality gates.
- **Directly applicable to the agent-harness work** (deepseek/prime harness items on the Mon nudge): every harness PR can ship a pseudocode description + test evidence as a standing rule — cheap to adopt, no new tooling required. For frontend-facing changes, @dctanner's Playwright-video + TTS narration is the heavyweight version of the same idea (the PR as demonstrable evidence).
- **Author overlap:** Pocock's /grill-me is step 1 of the Phelps planning loop captured the same day — plan-side and review-side bookends from the same community.
- **Skepticism gates:** it's a question tweet — the replies (28 at capture, not captured, login-walled) likely hold more techniques. /show-me carries no URL in the tweet body and remains unverified; @dctanner's technique is now fully captured (RDP-232) but unevaluated. Read the thread before adopting anything.
